sentence: The new regulation is ___: it protects workers but increases costs for small businesses.
explanation: <A double-edged sword> significa algo con ventajas y desventajas.
tip: Idiom with <sword>: ventajas y desventajas (3 words)

sentence: The invention of the smartphone was ___ in how we communicate.
explanation: <A watershed moment> significa un momento decisivo o punto de inflexión.
tip: Idiom with <watershed>: momento decisivo (3 words)

sentence: He tried to throw his colleague ___ to save his own job.
explanation: <Throw someone under the bus> significa traicionar a alguien por beneficio propio.
tip: Idiom with <bus>: traicionar a un colega (3 words)

sentence: I can't take on more work — I already ___.
correct: have a lot on my plate
explanation: <Have a lot on your plate> significa tener muchas responsabilidades.
tip: Idiom with <plate>: tener muchas responsabilidades (6 words)

sentence: If you think the delay is my fault, you're ___.
explanation: <Bark up the wrong tree> significa equivocarse de objetivo.
tip: Idiom with <tree>: equivocarse de objetivo (5 words, gerundio)

sentence: Discussing salaries at work can open ___.
explanation: <A can of worms> significa un tema complicado con muchos problemas ocultos.
tip: Idiom with <worms>: un tema complicado (4 words)

sentence: The manager decided to ___ to the employees' late arrivals.
explanation: <Turn a blind eye> significa ignorar algo deliberadamente.
tip: Idiom with <blind>: ignorar algo a propósito (4 words)

sentence: Everyone jumped ___ when the new trend became popular.
explanation: <Jump on the bandwagon> significa subirse a una moda o tendencia.
tip: Idiom with <bandwagon>: subirse a una moda (3 words)

sentence: Don't ___ with your business partners — you might need them again.
explanation: <Burn bridges> significa romper relaciones de forma definitiva.
tip: Idiom with <bridges>: romper relaciones (2 words)

sentence: We need to ___ to solve this creative challenge.
explanation: <Think outside the box> significa pensar de forma creativa.
tip: Idiom with <box>: pensar de forma creativa (4 words)

sentence: We're all ___ with these budget cuts.
explanation: <In the same boat> significa estar en la misma situación difícil.
tip: Idiom with <boat>: en la misma situación (4 words)

sentence: The project failed, so the team had to ___ and start again.
correct: go back to the drawing board
explanation: <Go back to the drawing board> significa volver a empezar desde cero.
tip: Idiom with <board>: volver a empezar (6 words)

sentence: Managers should nip small problems ___ before they grow into bigger ones.
explanation: <Nip something in the bud> significa cortar un problema de raíz.
tip: Idiom with <bud>: cortar un problema de raíz (3 words)

sentence: She'd agree to travel anywhere ___.
correct: at the drop of a hat
explanation: <At the drop of a hat> significa sin pensarlo, al instante.
tip: Idiom with <hat>: al instante, sin pensarlo (6 words)

sentence: Stop ___ and tell me what really happened.
explanation: <Beat around the bush> significa andarse con rodeos.
tip: Idiom with <bush>: andarse con rodeos (4 words, gerundio)

sentence: The media tends to blow small incidents ___.
explanation: <Blow something out of proportion> significa exagerar algo.
tip: Idiom with <proportion>: exagerar algo (3 words)

sentence: We need to ___ this issue before it affects the whole company.
explanation: <Get to the bottom of> significa llegar al fondo de un asunto.
tip: Idiom with <bottom>: llegar al fondo de un asunto (5 words)

sentence: Several new products are ___ for next year.
explanation: <In the pipeline> significa en preparación.
tip: Idiom with <pipeline>: en preparación (3 words)

sentence: The accountant ___ all company expenses closely.
explanation: <Keep tabs on> significa vigilar o hacer seguimiento de algo.
tip: Idiom with <tabs>: vigilar de cerca (3 words)

sentence: His sudden resignation ___ among his colleagues.
explanation: <Raise eyebrows> significa causar sorpresa o sospecha.
tip: Idiom with <eyebrows>: causar sorpresa (2 words, pasado)
